turns: I have an interview for the Product Operations Manager role at Clover Health on Thursday. prep me
replies:
Good — we'll prepare a tight, interview-ready kit for Product Operations Manager at Clover Health for Thursday.

Assumptions I made: the interview is in English, ~45–60 minutes, and you want spoken answers suitable for a hiring panel. If that’s off, tell me.
1) One-line purpose you can start with (60s "Tell me about yourself")
"I lead product operations by turning strategy into measurable execution: I partner with product and design to set clear success metrics, run experiments and dashboards, and unblock cross-functional delivery. In my last role I built an experimentation framework that increased feature launch velocity 30% and lifted user retention by 6 percentage points over six months. I focus on scalable processes, data-driven prioritization, and clear stakeholder communication — I want to bring that to Clover to help the product teams run faster, safer experiments and make decisions that improve member outcomes."
2) Three STAR stories you should memorize (short bullets, add numbers from your experience)
- Team win (Leadership + Execution)
  Situation: [Product area/problem you worked on]
  Task: Align PMs, design and analytics to ship a new onboarding flow.
  Action: Created a kickoff template, weekly dashboard, and a decision rubric; ran experiments with three cohorts.
  Result: Reduced time-to-onboard by [X% or X days], increased activation by [Y%]. (Put your exact numbers in the brackets.)
- Hard problem (Cross-functional unblock)
  Situation: A complex feature stalled due to unclear data ownership and dependencies.
  Task: Unblock delivery and define measurement.
  Action: Mapped dependencies, ran a two-week rapid sync with owners, negotiated a phased launch and a minimal telemetry plan.
  Result: Delivered MVP one month earlier than original estimate; early metrics matched predicted targets (give the percentage or numbers).
- Failure + learning (shows growth)
  Situation: An A/B test failed and we rolled it out prematurely.
  Task: Reassess why predictive signals misled us and restore trust in experimentation.
  Action: Led a retrospective, revised the experiment design checklist, added pre-launch metric guards, and retrained PMs.
  Result: Experiment quality score rose from [A to B], and subsequent launches met expected statistical power 90% of the time. (Add your exact metrics.)
3) Product-sense practice (structure to use: Clarify goal, constraints, metrics, propose solution, trade-offs)
- Question to practice aloud 1: “Design a way to measure and increase member engagement in Clover’s care apps. What metrics do you pick and what experiments would you run first?”
- Question 2: “A product team proposes a new feature that could improve retention but demands large engineering effort. How do you evaluate whether to prioritize it?”
- Question 3: “You only have access to coarse claims data and event logs. How would you decide if an observed improvement is real or noise?”
4) Execution / metrics practice (be specific: baseline, target, how you measure)
- Question 1: “How would you set KPIs and an OKR for a cross-functional initiative to reduce readmissions?”
- Question 2: “A dashboard shows a 4% drop in daily active users after a release. How do you investigate and communicate this to stakeholders?”

5) Two estimation / scoping prompts to rehearse
- “Estimate how many active members Clover serves in a typical city and how that shapes your sample size for an A/B test.”
- “Roughly estimate the time and roles needed to run an experiment that requires a new backend event, a UI change, and analytics tracking.”
6) Two smart questions to ask them at the end (team + work)
- "How is Product Operations currently structured at Clover, and which teams will I partner with most closely in the first 90 days?"
- "What are the top process or measurement gaps you want the new Product Operations Manager to close in the next six months?"

7) How to say "Why Clover Health" (two sentences)
"I want to work at Clover because you combine care delivery with product-driven experimentation to improve outcomes — that's where operations and measurement make an outsized difference. I'm excited to help scale processes and metrics that let clinicians, product and design iterate faster while protecting member outcomes."
8) Practical prep checklist (do these before Thursday)
- Ask the recruiter today: length, interviewers’ names and roles, format (behavioral, case, take-home), and the meeting link/time zone. (This brief said there’s no record of Clover rounds.)
- Bring your three stories with exact numbers filled in. Replace bracketed numbers above with your real metrics now.
- Test audio/video and screen-sharing; have a clean, quiet background and a second device with the job posting open.
- Prepare one-sheeter: 1-paragraph pitch, 3 bullets of impact (numbers), 3 gaps you’d fix in first 90 days.
9) Mock offer: run a timed mock with me
Text exactly: "mock me for Product Operations Manager at Clover Health" and I’ll ask the first question. After each answer you give, I’ll score it and ask the next.

Next step for me: Do you want me to run the timed mock now? (If yes, say that exact sentence.)

failed: prep tied to that posting's actual requirements
asks the first practice question or gives a concrete plan
judge.note: Good, targeted interview kit with strong behavioral and execution guidance, but it did not tie recommendations specifically to Clover Health's posting details (member experience, embed-with-floor responsibilities, change management, AI in member experience) and it did not ask the first practice question or provide the concrete plan promised.
